posts.title: Large-Format Masks Move From Aspiration To Industry Roadmap
posts.summary:
Expert panel sees a compelling productivity case, but the entire photomask ecosystem must be ready together.
The post Large-Format Masks Move From Aspiration To Industry Roadmap appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Industry consensus is shifting toward the adoption of 12-inch large-format photomasks, with a pilot line targeted for 2031 to support next-generation lithography.
The transition is driven by the need for higher productivity in High-NA EUV systems, as larger masks allow for bigger exposure fields without the complexity of A/B stitching.

Unlike previous failed attempts to standardize larger masks, this initiative is backed by major players including Intel, TSMC, and ASML, signaling a clear demand-driven shift in the semiconductor manufacturing roadmap.

posts.title: Vertical DRAM Stacking Expands Thermal Design Space Beyond HBM-on-GPU (imec)
posts.summary:
Researchers at imec published “Beyond HBM-on-GPU: Thermal Design Envelope for 3D Volumetric DRAM-on-GPU Integration.” Summary: Researchers evaluated a 3D memory architecture that rotates DRAM dies vertically above a GPU and places cooling cavities between them as an alternative to conventional 2.5D HBM and direct-stacked HBM-on-GPU. Package-level thermal simulations examined stack height, memory capacity and organization,... » read more
The post Vertical DRAM Stacking Expands Thermal Design Space Beyond HBM-on-GPU (imec) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Imec researchers have evaluated a 3D volumetric DRAM-on-GPU integration architecture that utilizes vertical die stacking and cooling cavities as an alternative to traditional 2.5D HBM.
The study utilized package-level thermal simulations to analyze variables including stack height, memory organization, and the integration of a distributed memory-controller/network-on-chip tier.
This research aims to overcome the thermal limitations inherent in current HBM-on-GPU configurations, potentially enabling higher memory density and performance for future AI-driven hardware.

posts.title: The End of the Internet
posts.summary: The old Internet, where anyone could host a server is over, but it's just the final blow in an ending that has been coming for years. The future, though, is brighter than it appears.
bullets: The evolution of web infrastructure, from manual PHP and MySQL configuration to managed services like Automattic's Pressable, reflects a broader shift toward professionalized, secure hosting environments.
The early 2000s marked a golden era of independent blogging, characterized by a decentralized explosion of political and niche content that defined the internet's first major transformation.
The recent discovery of a critical remote code execution vulnerability in PHP underscores the increasing complexity and security risks inherent in maintaining legacy web architectures.

The transition from the 'do-it-yourself' era of the early web to today's managed ecosystems highlights the loss of the internet's original open, experimental nature in favor of stability and security.

posts.title: Xpeng starts global shipments of Mona L05, targeting 65 countries and regions
posts.summary:
The Mona L05 will launch in China on October 29, with global shipments beginning ahead of its domestic roll-out.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: - The Mona L05 will launch in China on October 29, with global shipments beginning ahead of its domestic roll-out.
- Xpeng developed left- and right-hand-drive versions in parallel and says it deployed 660 vehicles for extreme-condition testing across 25 countries and regions.
Xpeng (NYSE: XPEV) has begun global shipments of the Mona L05, with plans to sell the SUV in 65 countries and regions as it prepares for its China launch.
The Chinese electric vehicle maker announced the move on Weibo on Monday, and reiterated that it will hold a "Mona World" owners' gathering and the L05's China launch event on October 29.
The move puts global shipments ahead of the Mona L05's official launch in China.
